sentences: Directed reachability asks whether a path exists from a specified start vertex to a specified target.
A graph search can solve it in polynomial time using substantial memory, while recursive reachability methods save memory at a time cost.
The question asks for one algorithm that simultaneously uses polynomial time and only polylogarithmic space.
Obtaining the two resource bounds in separate algorithms does not meet this requirement.
The problem is a basic test of whether reachability can combine efficient exploration with an extremely small working memory.
